reuse.why: setZero, the new setLastMonthSpending and the N-month averages use the new getBulkBudgetCategories, but copyPreviousMonth keeps its own inline hidden/#fixed/template checks instead of using it.

duplication.why: The month-wide exclusion rule is written twice, as SQL plus a tag filter in getBulkBudgetCategories and as inline JS checks in copyPreviousMonth (which also gains extra joined columns to support them).

placement.why: Selection logic and the new action live in budget/actions.ts and the handler is registered in budget/app.ts like its siblings.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps: exclusions, the new action, the #fixed rule and the hidden flag.

maintainability.why: A maintainer must keep two copies of the exclusion rule in sync, and they already diverge: copyPreviousMonth does not honour includeHiddenCategories; long inline option types are repeated per action.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth filters budget rows with its own hidden/group_hidden, #fixed and goal_def checks instead of calling getBulkBudgetCategories.

disguised_duplication.where: The exclusion rule in getBulkBudgetCategories (SQL WHERE + extractTagsFromText filter) is restated in copyPreviousMonth as separate early-return conditions over differently fetched columns.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories gains includeHiddenCategories; copyPreviousMonth re-implements the hidden, #fixed and template rules outside the helper and never receives the flag.
